description: Somos jóvenes apasionados por la astronomía e integrantes de HANANspace, organización dedicada a la divulgación científica en Perú.
summary:
We have developed "Silicon Heroes Tales," an interactive platform designed to help children aged 10 to 14 understand and draw inspiration from the history of space exploration.
In Lima, it is common to find children fascinated by space sciences. However, finding accessible learning resources can be challenging for them. Introductory materials often lack depth, while advanced content is technical and frequently available only in English. This gap makes young learners abandon the idea of ​​a future in space exploration.
To address this problem, "Silicon Heroes Tales" offers a look at past space missions through interactive maps and chronological storytelling. Beyond stating facts, the platform explores each mission’s development, challenges faced, discoveries, and its lasting legacy. Furthermore, by providing these experiences in Spanish, we aim to make space exploration more accessible, engaging, and inspiring for the next generation.
details:
How does Silicon Heroes Tales work?

Silicon Heroes Tales is an interactive educational platform designed for students aged 10 to 14. It offers two modes: “Interactive Stories” and “3D Planetarium and 2D Map.”

The first mode includes a series of integrated stories of a set of missions categorized into chapters according to different stages in the space exploration of the Moon and Mars. Each story is narrated through messages from the spacecraft and equipment themselves.

On the other hand, the second mode allows users to freely explore across the maps of the Moon and Mars and select the missions that interest them most.

In both modes, although our focus is storytelling, the user always has the opportunity to access technical information about each mission.

Intended impact

Through our organization, HANANspace, we plan to bring Silicon Heroes Tales to schools across Lima, making space science more accessible and engaging for young students. Having already reached more than 100 students through our outreach activities, we aim to expand our impact by introducing an interactive learning experience that sparks curiosity, strengthens scientific interest, and inspires the next generation of space explorers.

Behind the platform: How was it built?

The project is developed using a 100% open, lightweight web architecture that requires no installation, and is structured around three main engines:

Planetary (3D) and cartographic (2D) visualization engine:

In 3D mode, Three.js (WebGL) is used to render the Solar System, featuring the eight planets in dynamic orbits, alongside interactive globes of the Moon and Mars, rendered with realistic surface textures. Furthermore, real geographic coordinates (longitude and latitude) were converted into Cartesian vectors (x, y, z) to ensure greater precision across the spheres of these celestial bodies.

In 2D mode, an equirectangular cartographic engine, built using HTML5 Canvas, renders maps featuring a grid of meridians and parallels spaced every 30 degrees. Much like in 3D mode, it supports free zooming and panning.

Voice Synthesis and Adaptive Narrative Engine:

A narrator was implemented that detects natural-sounding Spanish voices available on the user's device, allowing for the playback, pausing, and repetition of each piece of dialogue in the story.

Factors of consideration

  • The target audience consists of students aged 10 to 14, who do not necessarily have any prior knowledge of astronomy.
  • Our platform prioritizes ease of understanding and simplicity of use over an overabundance of tools.
  • We focus on telling integrated stories from various space missions and grouping equipment according to different stages of space exploration.
  • We aim to highlight humanity’s progress in space exploration and its impact on us as a civilization.
